Dashboard: CODARIS Databases & Data Platforms Research Dataset

IMPORTANT TAXONOMY: MongoDB and PostgreSQL are database engines/DBMS products; MongoDB Atlas and Neon are managed services/platforms; Firebase is a developer platform whose database products include Firestore and Realtime Database; Supabase is a development platform built around PostgreSQL. CODARIS should keep these distinctions visible rather than labelling everything simply 'database'.

POPULARITY METRICS: Stack Overflow measures self-reported developer usage. DB-Engines is a monthly popularity index using multiple signals. Neither is a census or literal market share. Do not average these columns into one universal score.

Methodology: Issue
CODARIS treatment
Why
What counts as a database?
Catalogue database engines, managed database services, warehouses, embedded databases, search/vector data systems and developer data platforms, but preserve Product Type and Primary Model.
Developers commonly choose among all of these, but they are architecturally different layers.
DB-Engines ranking
Show rank and score only as DB-Engines popularity index values, dated September 2026.
The score is generated from several popularity signals and is not a percentage of developers or deployments.
Stack Overflow usage
Show 2025 'Have Used' percentage only for environments with verified published values.
The database question had 26,083 respondents and allowed multiple selections.
Firebase
Treat Firebase as a developer platform; list Cloud Firestore and Firebase Realtime Database as the actual database products.
Avoids presenting a platform brand and its databases as if they were one engine.
Supabase / Neon / PlanetScale
Classify as managed developer/database platforms and retain their PostgreSQL, Vitess/MySQL or other foundations.
Users need to understand whether they are selecting a database engine or an operational platform around one.
Search and vector systems
Include systems such as Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Pinecone, Milvus, Qdrant and Weaviate, labelled by type.
Modern application data architectures increasingly use search/vector stores alongside transactional databases.
Country data
Do not infer per-database country shares from overall respondent geography.
A country's representation in a survey does not establish database usage in that country.
Gender data
Leave per-database gender values blank unless an explicit cross-tab with sample sizes is available.
Prevents fabricated demographic precision and preserves non-binary/non-response categories.
Completeness
Call this an extensive curated catalogue of 643 entries, not 'every database ever made'.
DB-Engines alone tracks 438 DBMS products, while platforms/services create additional naming and taxonomy complexity.
